findings.category: cfunc exception handling / NRT refcount leak at the C boundary
findings.title: UDAF @cfunc callbacks have no exception guard; a raise inside an impl is swallowed by numba's cfunc boundary, leaking the borrow_structref incref and handing DuckDB a silent zero/void default
findings.description: Every DuckDB aggregate callback is a thin @cfunc wrapper that forwards to a module-level @njit impl with no try/except: _irr_state_size_cb (109-111), _irr_init_cb (124-126), _irr_update_cb (165-167), _irr_combine_cb (188-190), _irr_finalize_cb (209-211), _irr_destroy_cb (223-225). Per the codebase's own numba contract (MEMORY reference_numba_cfunc_swallows_exceptions: numba @cfunc returns the zero default and does NOT unwind to C on a Python exception, and NRT refs held across a raising call are leaked), any exception escaping an impl is silently converted to a 0/void return at the DuckDB boundary. Concretely: _irr_update_impl (156-157) and _irr_combine_impl / _irr_finalize_impl hold a live +1 from borrow_structref (numbox meminfo.py:131-140) at the moment they call vector_push / vector_extend, whose growth path allocates via numpy.empty (numbox vector.py:123,137); if that allocation raised, numba tears the frame down without the scope-exit decref, so the borrow's incref leaks (the group's MemInfo never reaches refcount 0, so its structref + the two Float64Vector heap buffers are never freed) AND the partially-updated aggregate is returned to DuckDB as success with no error signalled. _irr_state_size_cb returning the zero default would be catastrophic (0-byte state slot), though its body cannot actually raise. For realistic (non-OOM) inputs no impl raises, so the export(+1)/release(-1) ladder stays balanced -- this is a latent robustness gap, not an active miscount.
findings.impact: On an allocation failure (or any future edit that introduces a raising call into an impl), the C boundary silently swallows the error: the borrow_structref +1 leaks the group's MemInfo and its nested vector buffers, the DuckDB aggregate result is silently wrong/partial, and no rc/error is propagated to DuckDB or the caller. The failure is invisible until a downstream NRT alloc!=free check (irr.py:372-377) trips.
findings.recommendation: Wrap each impl body in a bare try/except (the documented cure -- do NOT use try/finally, which re-raises on numba 0.65.1) so the frame runs its NRT cleanup on the error path and the callback returns a defined default; for callbacks where a failure must be visible, surface it (e.g. leave the finalize output at math.nan, and prefer duckdb_aggregate/scalar error-signalling APIs over a silent zero). At minimum add a comment at each @cfunc wrapper noting the swallow-on-raise contract so future edits do not introduce an uncaught raising call across a held borrow_structref incref.

notes: Scope: how numbduck USES numbox at the UDAF state bridge (examples/irr.py) plus the pybridge string/pointer handoff, read against numbox meminfo.py/lowlevel.py/vector.py/highlevel.py. (1) REFCOUNTING IS BALANCED. The IRR UDAF performs exactly one export_meminfo(+1) per group in init (irr.py:119) and exactly one release_meminfo(-1) per group in destroy (irr.py:220); every borrow_structref in update/combine/finalize (irr.py:156,178-179,201) is net-0 (entry incref balanced by the impl's scope-exit decref). removerefctpass does not disturb this: each impl calls a function returning a refcounted structref (borrow_structref / the IRRState & Float64Vector ctors) so _legalize's valid_output gate is False and the pass is DISABLED in-frame, leaving both the increfs and the scope-exit decrefs intact -- the same mechanism the understanding note (udaf.md sec.5) verifies empirically via the NRT alloc==free guard at irr.py:372-377. Empty-group (finalize n==0 -> NaN, irr.py:203-204) and abort-before-finalize (destroy still runs) paths remain balanced. (2) INTRINSIC CONTRACTS RESPECTED. Every _cast_int_to_void_p argument (state, states, out_data, source/target, state_slots[iu]) is a genuine intp (cfunc intp args, intp-typed carray elements, or intp-returning ducklib wrappers), and _deref_structref_raw_ptr is reached only via borrow_structref with irr_state_type + a live intp meminfo pointer -- within _require_intp's contract. state_size is 8 == sizeof(intp) and only meminfo_p is stored/read (correct for the structref reconstruct-from-meminfo pattern); slot and states carray decodes are in-bounds against DuckDB's per-row/per-group state-array contract; finalize's out_vals is sized offset+count and written [offset,offset+count). (3) VECTOR len SEMANTICS CHECKED. Float64Vector(64) is capacity-64/size-0 (vector.py:84-89), and len() returns v.size (vector.py:96-101), so finalize's n=len(s.cashflows) is the true pushed count, not capacity -- no uninitialized-buffer read. (4) PYBRIDGE STRING LIFETIME CHECKED AND SOUND. get_unicode_data_p("SELECT 1") (pybridge.py:66) returns a pointer into the numba-unboxed unicode's data, which aliases the CPython buffer of the "SELECT 1" literal; that literal is a co_const of extract_connection_ptr so the buffer outlives the duckdb_query call -- not a dangling read. The result numpy buffer is held in a local for both the query and destroy calls. The raw pybind11 offset reads (+16/+32) are CPython objects that do not move and are validated; that is an ABI-portability risk documented in bridge.md, not a MEM-refcount/lifetime defect at the numbox boundary. Net: the numbox-boundary memory model is correct for realistic inputs on the 64-bit Linux target; the sole finding is the OOM-gated cfunc-swallow robustness gap (MEM-1).
